A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiKE method and FINE-KED benchmark. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reorganization and added evaluations.

before.justification: v1 reports original FINE-KED and COUNTERFACT experiments, component ablations, batch-editing evaluations, sensitivity analyses, and generation examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds multi-hop evaluation, generalization analyses, runtime comparisons, and additional generation examples.

M1.justification: The KRD disentangler/recomposer, three training losses, target-related representation editing, preservation constraints, and closed-form parameter update remain unchanged. Expanded training-versus-editing explanations describe the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MQUAKE-3K evaluation requiring two-, three-, and four-hop reasoning over edited facts (Appendices D.3 and G.2). This substantially extends task coverage beyond the retained FINE-KED and COUNTERFACT evaluations. The new seen/unseen analysis partitions existing FINE-KED coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds FT-L and MEND to the preliminary preservation comparison, and Figure 4 adds MEND to subject-consistent batch editing. Main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Figure 9's MEMIT-to-AlphaEdit caption correction matches the comparator already displayed in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds zero-shot multi-hop evaluation using edited-versus-original answer probabilities, four-way grouping by subject/relation exposure during KRD pretraining, and runtime measurement across batch sizes. These extend the evaluation design; existing training settings, COUNTERFACT sampling, and subject-consistent batch sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine generalization across seen/unseen subjects and relations, runtime scalability, and two additional generation cases presented as generalization evidence. Appendix D.1 also reports expert validation of difficulty labels, although agreement is only described qualitatively. Existing ablations, sample-size analyses, and representation visualization are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that reported results average five runs with different random seeds. v2 adds no numerical uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, formal significance tests, or quantified annotation-agreement statistics.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including MQUAKE scores of 44.39 for DiKE versus 41.28 for ROME (Table 10), subgroup results (Table 11), runtimes, and MEND batch-editing curves. Reported per-edit times change from 8/21/35 seconds to 2.79/8.72/11.34 seconds without explanation, so they do not establish a demonstrated speedup. Main FINE-KED and COUNTERFACT scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and closed-form derivations are retained, including Equations (1)–(29), with v1 Appendix D becoming v2 Appendix C. The added scalability discussion provides informal arguments rather than a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: disentanglement-based editing, improved fine-grained knowledge preservation, a closed-form update, and the FINE-KED benchmark. Additional evaluations support these claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of MEND's batch-editing failures, DiKE's scalability, and generalization to unseen knowledge patterns. Its limitations replace the warning about KRD pretraining-data and hyperparameter sensitivity with discussion of the restricted shared-subject definition of fine-grained irrelevant knowledge. The central entanglement explanation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, training data construction, hyperparameters, extraction layers, and optimization details are largely retained. v2 revises per-edit timings, adds batch runtime documentation, and introduces a reproducibility statement promising future code and FINE-KED release; it does not provide a project access link or establish actual release.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to MQUAKE and KELE and more explicitly attributes the least-squares formulation to MEMIT. Most expanded main-text related work already appeared in v1 Appendix C, so its relocation does not constitute a substantial positioning change.

P1.justification: Most methodological and experimental prose is retained. Changes include targeted clarification, moving detailed related work into Section 5, reorganizing appendices, and adding acknowledgements, ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands and revises the displays: four new tables, a reworked Figure 1, clearer phase labels and caption in Figure 2, revised plotting styles and axes, and Figure 9 expanded from three to five cases. Existing tables and figures are also redistributed within the conference layout.

improvement.justification: Multi-hop results, explicit subject/relation generalization analysis, and comparative runtimes strengthen evidence beyond v1's benchmarks and overlap percentages. The gain is limited by unspecified subgroup sizes, unquantified human validation, and unexplained timing revisions. Some interpretation also overreaches: Table 11's broad superiority statement overlooks AlphaEdit's 62.2 versus DiKE's 60.0 on middle-level locality for seen subjects and unseen relations.
